name: Lifelong Learning of Large Language Model based Agents: A Roadmap
authors: Junhao Zheng, Chengming Shi, Xidi Cai, Qiuke Li, Duzhen Zhang, Chenxing Li, Dong Yu, Qianli Ma (equal contribution by first four); lead affiliation: South China University of Technology (SCUT), with Tencent AI Lab and MBZUAI
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI), 2026; arXiv preprint 2501.07278 (v1 Jan 2025, v2 Jan 2026)
code_url: https://github.com/qianlima-lab/awesome-lifelong-llm-agent (curated literature/resource list, not a single method implementation)
reflection_type: none (survey). As an analysis object it taxonomizes reflection-related methods it reviews: verbal-self-critique (Reflexion), multi-agent-debate / model-feedback critics (N-CRITICS), tool-verified self-correction (CRITIC), and calibration/confidence-based intrinsic correction (If-or-Else prompting). Self-correction is treated as a Working-Memory sub-capability (Section 6.4) and experience-driven reflection as an Episodic/Reasoning-Action capability (Sections 7.3, 12).
feedback_source: n/a for the survey itself; it catalogues feedback sources used by reviewed works: self-generated verbal feedback, external-tool feedback (search engine, code interpreter via CRITIC), other-model critic feedback (N-CRITICS), environment reward/interaction feedback, and self-confidence assessment.
iteration_structure: n/a (survey). It organizes reviewed methods along single-trial vs multi-trial and intra-episodic vs inter-episodic axes, covering iterative-refine (self-correction), episodic-retry (Reflexion across trials), and tree/MCTS search (Tree of Thoughts, RAP, LLM-MCTS) approaches.
reflection_object: As a survey, it spans multiple objects across its three-module taxonomy: output content and reasoning chain (Working-Memory self-correction, Reasoning Actions), action trajectory and experience (Episodic Memory: self-experience, continual RL), prompt/context (Working-Memory prompt optimization, prompt compression), reusable skill/workflow (skill libraries, Agent Workflow Memory), external knowledge (Semantic Memory: knowledge graphs, documents), and model weights (Parametric Memory: continual instruction tuning, knowledge editing, alignment).
requires_training: n/a (survey). It explicitly covers the full spectrum of reviewed techniques: training-free in-context methods (prompting, self-correction, episodic experience reuse), continual SFT (continual instruction tuning), continual RL (continual reinforcement learning of agents), and continual alignment (preference/DPO-style updates) under the Parametric Memory module.
reward_or_critic_model: n/a (survey). It surveys multiple improvement signals among reviewed works: self-as-judge (intrinsic self-correction, confidence assessment), separate/other-model critics (N-CRITICS), external verifiable tools (CRITIC), and environment reward (continual RL).
distillation_target: n/a as a method; the survey frames where experience is consolidated across its memory taxonomy: episodic-memory (self-experience, replay), reusable-skill/workflow (skill libraries, Agent Workflow Memory/AWM), prompt (prompt optimization/compression), structured external knowledge (semantic memory / knowledge graphs), and model-weights (parametric memory).
emergent_vs_engineered: Mostly surveys scaffold/prompt-engineered reflective behaviors (Reflexion, CRITIC, N-CRITICS, self-correction prompting, skill libraries). The v1 (Jan 2025) framing predates wide adoption of RL-emergent reasoning; reinforcement-learning-based self-evolution is discussed primarily as a future direction (Section 15.3, 'Reinforcement Learning for Self-Learning and Evolution') rather than centered on R1-style emergent reflection.
memory_type: Surveys all categories. Its central contribution is a four-type memory taxonomy: Working Memory (short-term/scratchpad), Episodic Memory (long-term-episodic experience), Semantic Memory (external structured-notes/knowledge-graph/document store), and Parametric Memory (knowledge stored in model weights). Also covers skill-library / workflow memory under action and reasoning modules.
memory_persistence: Covers the full range: within-episode (working memory), cross-episode and cross-task (episodic/semantic memory, continual learning), and toward cross-session production deployment. The survey's explicit goal is cross-task / lifelong persistence that mitigates catastrophic forgetting across an agent's lifetime.
memory_curation_mechanism: Surveys multiple curation strategies and flags memory growth as an open challenge (Section 15.2 'Dynamic Memory Management'): append-only experience stores, self-summarized/curated memory, replay buffers (data/feature replay), retrieval-gated access (retrieval actions over semantic/episodic memory), knowledge distillation for consolidation, and proactive pruning/summarization of outdated knowledge. Neuro-inspired consolidation is proposed as a future direction.
error_localization_granularity: n/a as a single method; the survey reviews methods spanning holistic/outcome-level (trial-level Reflexion), response-level self-correction (N-CRITICS, CRITIC), and step-level reasoning correction (Tree of Thoughts, RAP, MCTS-based reasoning actions). No single localization granularity is proposed.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: Both, and this is an explicit organizing axis of the survey. Section 12 distinguishes Intra-Episodic Reasoning Actions (single-trial and across-trial within a task, e.g. ReAct, Reflexion, Tree of Thoughts) from Inter-Episodic Reasoning Actions (transfer of experience across tasks/episodes, e.g. ICAL, GITM, Voyager). The lifelong-learning framing emphasizes inter-task / cross-episode experience transfer.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: Surveys both: avoidance via cross-trial reflection (Reflexion reflects on past failed trials to improve the next trial), mid-trajectory recovery via in-flight self-correction (CRITIC, N-CRITICS revise current output using tool/critic feedback), and post-hoc revision. The lifelong lens stresses accumulating experience to avoid repeating failures across episodes.
task_domains: Broad coverage: web-navigation, embodied/games (Minecraft via Voyager/GITM), tool-use, QA/reasoning, code, dialogue, role-playing, decision-making, plus domain-specific applications in education, law, and medicine. Organized around perception (web/charts/games, multimodal), memory, and action (grounding/retrieval/reasoning).
benchmarks: Catalogues benchmarks in two groups. Simple/skill-specific continual-learning: CITB, GLUE, SuperGLUE, NaturalInstructions/SuperNI, WMT, TED Talks, CLLE, zsRE, FEVER, CounterFact, Concept-1K, Biography. Complex agent environments: ToolBench, StableToolBench, APIBench, ToolAlpaca, API-Bank, WebArena, WebShop, WorkArena, VisualWebArena, VideoWebArena, AgentBench, VisualAgentBench, Mind2Web, plus game environments (Minecraft).
headline_result: Survey/roadmap with no single quantitative headline; it claims to be the first to systematically organize lifelong-learning techniques for LLM-based agents into a perception / memory / action three-module framework, and contributes a unified taxonomy plus lifelong-learning evaluation metrics (AP, AIP, FGT, BWT, FWT).
baselines: n/a (survey). Positions itself against prior surveys it cites, notably Zheng et al. 'Towards Lifelong Learning of Large Language Models: A Survey' (arXiv 2406.06391) and a continual-learning-for-LLMs survey by Shi et al., arguing those treat LLMs as static black boxes without environment interaction, whereas this survey centers agent-environment interaction.
gains_vs_baseline: n/a (no empirical comparison; survey/roadmap). It does not report performance deltas; instead it formalizes lifelong-learning metrics by which agents could be compared: Average Performance (AP), Average Incremental Performance (AIP), Forgetting Measure (FGT), Backward Transfer (BWT), and Forward Transfer (FWT).
compute_cost_profile: n/a (survey). It discusses compute/scaling qualitatively as open challenges (scalable memory architectures, ever-growing memory volume, dynamic memory management) but reports no inference-token multipliers or training-cost figures.
known_limitations: As stated for the field/survey: catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity (the stability-plasticity dilemma) remain unsolved; perception fails on novel distributions/modalities; memory does not scale gracefully (growth, retrieval, pruning); tree/MCTS reasoning methods unrealistically assume states are retraceable (e.g. irreversible web payments); lack of standardized, realistic, reproducible benchmarks and unified evaluation. As a survey it is a roadmap rather than an empirical contribution, so claims are not experimentally validated here.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: n/a as a method; the survey explicitly distinguishes feedback sources among reviewed self-correction works: intrinsic-only / self-verify (If-or-Else confidence-based intrinsic self-correction), other-model critics (N-CRITICS), and external-tool/verifier dependence (CRITIC using search engine / code interpreter), plus environment-reward via continual RL. It does not adjudicate the Huang/Kamoi 'self-correction needs oracle' critique.
self_correction_efficacy: task-dependent (as surveyed). The survey presents self-correction as a working-memory capability that improves outputs via iterative feedback (self, other-model, or tool), without quantifying when intrinsic correction fails; it does not take a strong empirical position on net-positive vs net-negative correction.
calibration_effect: not-measured. The survey discusses confidence self-assessment (If-or-Else intrinsic self-correction) as a self-correction strategy but does not analyze calibration improvement/degradation or a 'reasoning tax'.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (the survey is a roadmap, not a failure-attribution method). It addresses failure conceptually via catastrophic forgetting and loss of plasticity and via reflection-on-failed-trials (Reflexion) but provides no failure-attribution taxonomy or responsible-agent/step localization.
failure_mode_addressed: Primary failure modes framed at the field level: catastrophic forgetting (loss of past knowledge) and loss of plasticity (inability to adapt) — the stability-plasticity dilemma. Reviewed reflection methods (Reflexion) target repeating past mistakes by reflecting on failed trials; relation to MAST's 14 multi-agent failure modes is not addressed.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset or benchmark released. The contribution is a curated, continuously updated resource/literature repository (awesome-lifelong-llm-agent on GitHub) and a survey-level catalogue/categorization of existing benchmarks; no original traces or labeled failure dataset.
builds_on: Prior lifelong/continual-learning surveys for LLMs: Zheng et al. 'Towards Lifelong Learning of Large Language Models: A Survey' (arXiv 2406.06391, same first author); Shi et al. continual-learning-for-LLMs survey; classic continual-learning surveys (De Lange et al. TPAMI 2021; Wang et al. TPAMI 2024). Core agent methods it synthesizes: ReAct, Reflexion, Tree of Thoughts, Voyager, GITM, CRITIC, N-CRITICS, Agent Workflow Memory (AWM), ICAL, FireAct.
citation_count: 72 (Semantic Scholar API, paperId 76aebf01bdfeaf743ac83ac231384a861f7b69ca, retrieved 2026-06-08; influential citation count 2)
reasoning_model_native: Not specifically targeted. The v1 framing (Jan 2025) precedes broad reasoning-model adoption; RL-driven self-evolution is treated as a future direction (Section 15.3) rather than a study of o1/R1-style models with built-in reflection. The v2 (Jan 2026) revision may update this, but the core taxonomy is model-agnostic and centers on external memory/action scaffolding rather than native reasoning models.
on_policy_distillation_link: Indirect. Knowledge distillation and replay are surveyed as consolidation mechanisms for the memory module, and continual RL / experience reuse are discussed, but there is no explicit treatment of on-policy distillation or skill-optimization as a named technique.
sample_efficiency: n/a (survey reports no trials-to-gain measurements). It motivates lifelong learning partly by sample/efficiency arguments (reusing past experience for faster adaptation, 'Transfer Learning for Rapid Adaptation') but gives no quantitative sample-efficiency figures.
